name: Hunter eyes surgery

lead: Hunter eyes surgery is looksmaxxing shorthand for operations meant to give a deep-set, positively tilted, low-lid-show eye look. In practice it usually means canthopexy or canthoplasty, sometimes combined with fat grafting or blepharoplasty.
The surgical literature studies these procedures for lid support and rejuvenation, not for creating this look, so the aesthetic goal itself has no direct trial evidence.

paras: Canthal procedures reposition or suspend the outer lower eyelid and lateral canthus; fat grafting adds volume under the eye or brow; blepharoplasty reshapes lid tissue. Together they aim to change tilt and lid exposure.

Reviews describe lid malposition, scleral show, ectropion and shape changes as risks, noting that small changes around the canthus can have large effects. Results as a combined cosmetic package are only documented in forum posts.

lead: 'Hunter eyes' is looksmaxxing slang for an eye appearance usually described as deep-set, with little upper eyelid show, a low brow-to-lid distance, and a neutral or positive canthal tilt. 'Hunter eyes surgery' is the community term for surgical combinations intended to produce that look, most often canthopexy or canthoplasty at the outer eye corner, sometimes combined with fat grafting, brow or blepharoplasty procedures.[1]

There is no single standard operation by that name in the surgical literature. The components are established procedures with other indications: canthopexy and canthoplasty for lower-lid support, lower blepharoplasty, and fat transfer to the periorbital region.[2][3][4] Published studies assess these for lid position, rejuvenation and functional outcomes; no study located evaluates them as a package to create a 'hunter' look.

Canthopexy supports the lower eyelid, typically in conjunction with lower blepharoplasty to reduce the risk of lid malposition, and reviews describe it as the most conservative form of canthal suspension.[3][5] Because small changes around the lateral canthus can change eyelid shape substantially, reviews call for caution in this area.[3]

paras: In forum usage, 'hunter eyes' refers to eyes seen as intense or predatory, typified by a low lid-to-brow distance and a lateral corner that sits at or above the medial corner. The surgery associated with it is a bundle of procedures rather than one operation; a thread about one member's result describes 'various surgeries combined to get eyes that look as hunter as possible' and attributes the apparent brow elevation to fat grafting.[1]

Canthopexy suspends the lower eyelid to the lateral orbital rim with sutures, while canthoplasty involves detaching and reattaching the lateral canthal tendon. Reviews describe canthopexy as the most conservative option and canthoplasty as reserved for more marked laxity.[3] A 1993 article argued that canthopexy should be a routine companion or alternative to lower lid blepharoplasty, restoring lid tone and contour.[5] Anatomical work has mapped the ligamentous attachments of the lower lid and lateral canthus.[6]

Contemporary lower eyelid surgery increasingly includes repositioning of orbital fat to correct inferior orbital hollowing, correcting the negative vector and smoothing the lid-cheek junction.[2] A 10-year series of lower blepharoplasty with routine lateral canthal support is among the larger reports.[7]

Reviews describe lid malposition, scleral show, ectropion and entropion as the main complications of lower eyelid surgery and canthal work.[2][3][8] Reviews note that canthopexy or canthoplasty is used to reduce the risk of malposition after blepharoplasty.[3][7]

Human studies cover the component procedures in other contexts: a randomised trial of subciliary approaches and lower lid position in infraorbital rim fractures,[8] a randomised trial of lower eyelid blepharoplasty outcomes and patient satisfaction,[9] and surgeon case series on canthal support.[7][10] No study located assesses a combined 'hunter eyes' procedure or measures canthal tilt change as an aesthetic outcome.

Members debate canthopexy versus canthoplasty for tilt, with some stating canthopexy is preferable for younger patients, and one thread asks whether pulling the lateral corner adds millimetres of positive 'PFL' (palpebral fissure length).[11][12][13][12] Members also share before-and-after posts of combined surgeries.[1]

lore.intro: Hunter eyes are treated as a desirable aesthetic target in looksmaxxing, and surgery is discussed as a way to attain them for people without them naturally.[11][1]

claims.claim: Canthopexy can create hunter eyes or a more positive canthal tilt.
Combined surgeries, including fat grafting, produce a more hunter look than any one procedure.
Canthopexy adds millimetres of palpebral fissure length.
